title: Quantum Many-Body Metrology of Rotation Sensing with Strong Interactions
abstract: We study the ultimate quantum limit of rotation sensing with a few strongly interacting bosons confined in a quasi-one-dimensional ring trap with two weak links. It is demonstrated that a self-consistent many-body solution of the problem is required to correctly predict the ultimate sensitivity of this strongly correlated many-body gyroscope to rotation. For both small rotation velocities and small particle numbers, the many-body quantum Fisher information becomes maximal for large interaction couplings, showing the potential of strongly interacting miniaturized many-body sensors to precisely estimate slow rotations with high spatial resolution.
summary: This paper investigates enhancing rotation sensing sensitivity using strongly interacting bosons trapped in a quasi-1D ring. By employing advanced MCTDH calculations, the authors demonstrate that strong interactions beneficially increase the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) at zero rotation rate, significantly outperforming simpler mean-field approximations.
main_problem: The study focuses on determining the ultimate quantum limit for rotation sensing using strongly interacting bosonic systems.
main_result: Self-consistent many-body calculations show that strong interactions can enhance the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) at zero rotation rate, contrary to mean-field predictions.
method: The authors employ a fully self-consistent approach utilizing the Multi-Configurational Time-Dependent Hartree (MCTDH) method to compute the QFI of the full many-body eigenstates.
model_or_system: The system consists of strongly interacting bosons confined in a quasi-one-dimensional ring trap with two weak links. The dynamics are governed by a Hamiltonian incorporating interaction terms and an angular momentum term related to rotation.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), which sets the ultimate precision limit for estimating the rotation rate ($\Omega$).
important_parameters: Interaction coupling strength ($\lambda_{1D}$ or $\gamma$), particle number ($N$), and the ratio of interaction to kinetic energy.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing the full MCTDH solution against simpler approximations like the two-mode Bose-Hubbard model, which is shown to be insufficient for accurate metrology predictions.
figures_summary: Figures compare QFI results between the full MCTDH method and the simplified Bose-Hubbard model across varying interaction strengths and particle numbers. One figure shows the dependence of QFI on lattice depth.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical setup (interacting bosons in a ring trap) and the metrological goal (maximizing QFI). It then develops the theoretical framework using MCTDH, contrasting its results against simpler mean-field models to demonstrate the non-trivial enhancement provided by strong correlations.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses how strong quantum correlations can be harnessed in ultracold atomic systems to surpass classical or simple mean-field limits in precision sensing applications like gyroscopes.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Illustration of the rotation sensing setup. The interacting bosons are placed in a strongly confining ring trap, on which an azimuthal two-site optical lattice poten- tial V (θ) = V0 cos2 θ, breaking azimuthal invariance, is super- imposed (black), leading to localization of the single-particle density (blue) for large V0.

FIG. 2. The QFI for N = 2 bosons with coupling λ1D = 0.39 and V0/Er = 8. Dashed line is the BH result with fixed Wannier orbitals. Scattered points show MCTDH calculation results for M = 2 (circles) and M = 24 (triangles) orbitals. Lines are guides to the eye.
FIG. 3. Convergence of QFI for large coupling, for Ω= 0 (from below) and Ω0/2 (from above), with M = 2 and 24 self-consistently computed orbitals (N = 2).

FIG. 4. (a) Left panel: Lattice-depth dependence of the QFI at Ω= 0 for N = 2 interacting bosons. Right panel: Normalized one-body Glauber correlation function g(1) LR = g(1)(θ = π/2, θ′ = 3π/2) between the two azimuthal lattice sites. M = 8 orbitals were used for the self-consistent cal- culation. (b) Interaction-strength dependence of the QFI at Ω= 0 for N = 4 (left column) and N = 6 (right column) bosons. M = 12 (M = 18) orbitals were used for N = 4 (N = 6) to reach convergence.

FIG. 5. First row: Occupation entropy (16) as a function of coupling λ1D. The normalized one-body density ρ(θ) along the azimuthal direction is displayed in the second row for V0/Er = 8 (N = 4) and V0/Er = 11.2 (N = 6). M = 12 (M = 18) orbitals were used for N = 4 (N = 6).
